cluster.description: The name of the target Distributed Cloud Edge Cluster.
cluster.rationale: Identifier referencing the parent cluster for the node pool. We don't constrain references to other resources; which cluster a pool belongs to is a team structural choice, not a security control.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

labels.description:
Labels associated with this resource.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are metadata for organisation and billing on the node pool; they do not affect access, exposure, or encryption.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

machine_filter.description:
Only machines matching this filter will be allowed to join the node pool.
The filtering language accepts strings like "name=<name>", and is
documented in more detail in [AIP-160](https://google.aip.dev/160).
machine_filter.rationale: A free-form filter expression selecting which physical machines host node-pool nodes. The correct value is site/team-specific and cannot be generically constrained.

name.description: The resource name of the node pool.
name.rationale: Node pool name is an identifier and doesn't directly impact security.

node_count.description: The number of nodes in the pool.
node_count.rationale: Sets the number of nodes in the pool. This is capacity/scaling sizing, a team operational choice, and does not control access, exposure, or encryption.

node_location.description: Name of the Google Distributed Cloud Edge zone where this node pool will be created. For example: 'us-central1-edge-customer-a'.
node_location.rationale: Determines the geographic location where node-pool nodes run. A data-residency policy should require it to be in an approved location whitelist; region is the sanctioned case where a concrete allowed set is acceptable.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Specifies the GCP project the node pool belongs to. This is an identifier/reference that does not independently control access or security settings.

local_disk_encryption.description: Local disk encryption options. This field is only used when enabling CMEK support.

local_disk_encryption.kms_key.description:
The Cloud KMS CryptoKey e.g. projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{keyRing}/cryptoKeys/{cryptoKey} to use for protecting node local disks.
If not specified, a Google-managed key will be used instead.
local_disk_encryption.kms_key.rationale: Sets the CMEK used for local disk encryption on node-pool nodes. A policy should require it to be non-empty so node disks are always CMEK-encrypted; it must not pin a specific key, since keys are team/project-specific.

node_config.description: Configuration for each node in the NodePool

node_config.labels.rationale: Kubernetes node labels are metadata used for scheduling and organisation; they do not enforce access, exposure, or encryption controls.
